## Findings considered and refused

- **849 · n · hāton** ("must be a dative singular of hāt with an odd ending"). The reading of hāton as a mis-ended dative of hāt matches how the line has to be construed, and the note already says it is a variant spelling. Left.
- **889 · n · frēcne dǣde** ("accusative singular feminine; the verb may govern the dative, which looks the same"). For an i-stem feminine the accusative singular dǣd and the dative dǣde differ, so "looks the same" is loose, but I could not settle the case ending with certainty from the packet and lexica allowed; the sense is unaffected. Left; to be rechecked in pass 2 if someone can cite Klaeber’s glossary.
- **873 · l/i · gerāde** (l "rightly", adverb; i "a fitting tale", adjective). The note says openly that the form is uncertain, adjective or adverb, and a guess. Left.
- **873 · i · "ringing changes on his words"**. Idiom for wordum wrixlan ("to vary with words"); no recalled translation matches it and it is rebuilt from the verb, so left.
- **874 · n · wēlhwylc**. Reading ("he said every one" / "each said") is hedged in the note and now matches l. Left.
- **864 · i · "battle-bold riders"**. "Riders" is supplied by i; the note says the subject is the riders and heaþorōfe is the adjective used as a noun. Acceptable gloss. Left.
- **862 · l/i · glædne "glad" / "gracious"**. The note explains glæd as "bright, gracious". Left.
- **881 · i · "for they were always comrades"** (swā "as, since"). Causal reading is within the note’s "as, since". Left.
- **918 · l/i · swīðhicgende "strong-minded" / "stout-hearted"**. The note gives "strong-minded, resolute"; i is idiomatic and close in sense. Left.
- **856 · n · mǣrðo number** (singular collective or plural with singular verb). Honest hedge about a genuinely ambiguous form. Left.
- **902 · n · forlācen**. Flagged as a guess in the note, l and i; acceptable. Left.
- **904 · n · lemian "lame, cripple, here crush" vs i "crippled"**. Minor; "crippled" is within the note’s range. Left.
- **886 · n · "hē is understood"**. Reading wīges heard as the subject with hē supplied is a description of the English; harmless. Left.
- **853 · n · ealdgesīðas "the word is rare"**. Not checkable against the packet; harmless. Left.
- **913 · n · ēþel from the rune**. Reasoning is hedged ("a reading from the rune’s name, not a certainty") and fits the apparatus (913a MS. . ᛟ .). Left.
- **Names in l/i** (Hrothgar, Beowulf, Heremod, Sigemund, Wæls’s). Match published practice (fitt-01, 02, 06); only Higelac needed aligning.
- **Remembered English**: i was scanned for stock phrases. Only 898 ("by far the most famous", "shelter") sounded stock and was rebuilt; the rest is compositional. No modern translation was consulted.

# Review, pass 2 — beowulf-fitt-13 (lines 837–924)

Reviewer pass 2 of 2. Every grammatical label in every note was re-checked against its line, l against i, and the pass-1 edits for new faults (none found: the pass-1 rewrites at 867, 874, 889, 898, 913 and 917 all hold). Cross-references and line numbers in the notes (846, 863, 877, 879, 888, 897, 905, 917, 919) were checked against the packet and are right.

## Findings considered and refused

- **849 · n · hāton as a dative of an adjective at all (pass-1 refusal revisited).** Re-examined as asked. The alternatives (a verb form of hātan; a noun) do not parse: hātan "call" has preterite hēton, and nothing in the line governs a verb. The adjective-with-heolfre reading stands; only the justification was repaired (see 847).
- **850 · n · dēof.** Re-examined. Pass 1’s parse (fǣge nominative singular masculine, a ja-stem adjective; dēof the verb) is correct; the apparatus is quoted accurately (MS deog; dēag, dēog, dēop, dēaf; Tr.1 and Holt. dēof = dēaf); the note rightly calls the verb a guess and the l/i "dived" / "plunged" agree with it. "Klaeber’s dēof is said to equal dēaf" is accurate to the apparatus (Tr.1, Holt.). Left. The gloss entry, however, contradicted all of this; see below.
- **924 · l/i/n · medostigge.** Whether stigge is accusative or dative cannot be settled from the packet and public-domain aids at hand; the note now says so plainly instead of leaving a bare "uncertain". l ("the mead-path measured") and i ("walked the way to the mead-hall") agree with the accusative reading. i adds "to the mead-hall", an interpretation of "mead-path"; it matches the glossary gloss and is within the compound. Left.
- **889 · l/i · "a perilous deed" (singular) against the formal possibility of an accusative plural.** The poet is telling one exploit under the stone; the singular is the natural sense. Kept, with the plural named in the note.
- **847 · i · "all mixed with it".** "with it" is not in the Old English, but eal gemenged requires some stated material and the line continues with the gore. Left.
- **874 · l/i · wēlhwylc as object ("he said every one") against subject.** Hedged in the note; l follows the first reading, and the gloss now carries an accusative broadening for it. Left.
- **876 · n · "uncūþes fela ... much of the unknown".** Fine as a gloss of fela + genitive; l ("much unknown") is looser but follows the construction. Left.
- **879 · n · "mid here takes the accusative hine".** Correct as stated (mid with the accusative is the rarer construction); left.
- **888 · n · "the one meant is Wæls".** Right on the line: æþelinges bearn, then Wælses eafera at 897. Left.
- **902 · n · Ēotenum "probably the Jutes".** Hedged and standard; the note cites the apparatus for the variant spelling. Left.
- **905 · n · lemede singular with plural subject.** Already flagged in the note with the editors who emend. Left.
- **913 · n · mǣg Higelāces "in apposition" to Hē.** Correct. Left.
- **918–919 · l/i · swīðhicgende.** "strong-minded" / "stout-hearted" are within the note’s gloss and the house usage; swīðferhþes at 908 is "strong-minded" in l and "stern-minded" in i for a different word; no clash. Left.

## Checked and found true (no change)

Case/number labels checked against the line, all true: fērdon (past plural, folctogan subject); ǣnẹgum, secga (dative plural, genitive plural); tīrlēases (genitive singular); nīða ofercumen (genitive plural; phrase marked insecure); nicera; weallende; ȳða; drēama lēas; hǣþene sāwle; onfēng; gewiton; mōdge; mēarum; blancum; nǣre (subjunctive); twēonum; wyrðra with rīces; lōgon (strong class VI lēan); glædne; heaþorōfe; foldwegas; cūðe; cystum; gilphlæden; gidda; ealdgesegena; worn; word ōþer (singular, as ōþer is the neuter singular form); Sigemunde[s] and the apparatus names; ellendǣdum; Wælsinges; wīde sīðas; þāra þe; fǣhðe ond fyrena; ēam (nominative singular), nefan (dative singular; nominative plural in form only); nȳdgesteallan (predicate); eotena cynnes; Sigemunde (dative); dōm unlȳtel; wīges heard; hordes hyrde; hārne (accusative, motion with under); wrǣtlīcne; ætstōd; morðre (dative singular of morðor); selfes dōme; sǣbāt gehleōd (irregular preterite, apparatus 895b); wyrm hāt (agreeing or adverb); wreccena (partitive genitive); werþēode; wīgendra hlēo; onðāh; sweðrode; forlācen; lemede; swīðferhþes; bealwa; fæderæþelum; ēþel (rune reading hedged); gefægra; fyren onwōd; fealwe strǣte; scofen ond scynded; Ēode (singular with scealc monig); hēan (weak dative); tryddode; getrume micle; gecȳþed; hōse (dative); mægþa (genitive plural). l ↔ i agreement checked line by line after the edits; remaining differences are idiom, not sense. Spelling of names (Higelāc/Higelac, Hrōðgār, Heremōd, Sigemund, Wæls) matches the published parts. Published parallels checked by grep: Hwīlum ("At whiles" in l; "Sometimes"/"at times" in i), hlēo ("shelter"/"protector"), mǣg ("kinsman"), eafoð ond ellen ("strength and valor", now matched).

## Gloss check

gloss.json was read in full against the lines. Key set: it covers exactly novel-forms.json (no missing, no extra keys), plus a `__broaden__` section. Every `__broaden__` entry begins with the old entry from known-forms.json whole, then " · " and the new reading (checked by script, including the six added in this pass). No entry contains a line number or "here".

Wrong parses fixed (gloss.json entries; severity in brackets):

- **dēof** [medium]: entry said "dēogan — hid, lurked; some take ‘died’", which contradicts the unit note and l/i ("dived"). Now dūfan, 3rd singular preterite, strong II, the manuscript’s dēog and the other readings named, uncertainty stated.
- **dǣde** [medium]: "accusative plural feminine; object of genēðde" asserted one reading as fact and tied it to a line. Now: dative/genitive singular or nominative/accusative plural in form, so the case is uncertain, with the accusative and dative-of-manner readings given.
- **frēcne** [medium]: "accusative plural feminine" only; now accusative singular or plural feminine, or the adverb.
- **nefan** [medium]: "ēam his nefan ‘uncle and his nephew’; the case is disputed" disagreed with l and the note ("the uncle to his nephew", dative singular). Fixed.
- **hāton** [medium]: ending described as "odd" with no analysis; now dative singular neuter, -on for -um or -an, not the verb hātan.
- **gerāde** [medium]: "accusative singular neuter agreeing with spel" is not a form a strong neuter accusative takes; now adjective-or-adverb, uncertain, as in the note.
- **cūðe (broaden)** [medium]: the new reading said "agreeing with foldwegas", which contradicted the note (the horses) and tied the entry to the passage; now "nominative or accusative plural masculine".
- **hyrde (broaden added)** [medium]: the existing entry gives only the nominative; hordes hyrde at 887 is an accusative in apposition to wyrm, so a second reading was added.
- trode, medostigge [low]: case/gender asserted flatly (accusative singular; "feminine, accusative singular") though the notes say the case is uncertain; hedged to match.
- cystum [low]: "used adverbially" removed (it is a dative of respect/cause).
- feorhlāstas [low]: "fled for life" stated as the meaning; the note calls the sense a guess; hedged.
- gehleōd [low]: now says the spelling is irregular (gehlōd), as the note and apparatus do.
- genēðde [low]: "takes the accusative" removed (the case of its object is the open question at 889).
- mere [low]: dative or accusative are identical in form; stated.
- onðāh [low]: example said "by it" for þæs; now "before that", dispute noted, matching the note.
- rīces [low]: "takes after wyrðra" reworded.
- sǣm [low]: circular wording ("strong form for sǣm") replaced.
- brȳdbūre [low]: neuter removed (gender not certain from the aids permitted).
- heremōdes [low]: "driven out" is not in the text; now "turned to crime and was betrayed to his enemies".
- aldorceare, ǣnẹgum [low]: remark wording tidied; the dot is described as Klaeber’s sign for non-counting vowels.
- hāt, mǣrðo (broaden) [low]: "or adverbial" added to the first; number of mǣrðo left open, as in the note.
- scolde (broaden added) [low]: the existing readings (obligation; subjunctive in a condition) do not cover "trusted that he should thrive".
- wēlhwylc (broaden added) [low]: the existing entry gives only the nominative; the note’s main reading takes it as an accusative object.

Checked and left (parse true of the line): all other novel entries (for example fērdon, ealdgesīðas, gomenwāþe, mōdge, blancum, nicera, nīða, ofercumen, tīrlēases, uncūþes, gumena-bearn forms, wreccena, werþēode, wyrðra, sweðrode, lemede, fæderæþelum, hlēoburh, searowundor, gilphlæden, tryddode, hōse, mægþa, mæt).
